name: Vendor & Supply Chain Impersonation
description: Many organizations grant broad physical access to third-party vendors, contractors, delivery personnel, and maintenance crews with minimal verification. Impersonating a known vendor — an IT hardware supplier, a copier service technician, a HVAC contractor — can yield escorted access to server rooms, network closets, and executive floors that standard visitor procedures would not permit. Effective execution requires OSINT to identify actual vendors the target uses (job postings, LinkedIn, dumpster diving for invoices), construction of a plausible service visit pretext, and attire and props matching the vendor's real field technicians.

tools.name: Fake work order or service ticket

blue.det: Vendor not in approved vendor list; visit not pre-scheduled; inconsistencies in vendor documentation; camera footage of vendor accessing areas beyond stated scope.
blue.cm: Approved vendor list with pre-scheduled visit policy; vendor verification process (call vendor company directly, not the number they provide); vendor escort throughout facility; access limited strictly to area of stated work; visitor log with photo ID.
